A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PG-OT research work, with readable main text and complete appendices A–G. PDF pages 2–23 have identical extracted text and rendered pixels; page 1 differs only in affiliation information, version metadata, and typesetting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, a human study with ten annotators on 300 DiffusionDB prompts, component ablations, and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original benchmark, human-study, ablation, and supplementary results, including the quantitative outcomes in Tables 3–11.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A and D retain the same offline Pareto-frontier construction, VLM-based reward removal and checkpoint rollback, and online optimal-transport optimization. No algorithmic component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Pick-High training prompts, Pick-a-Pic/Pick-High reward-model evaluation, Parti-Prompts benchmarking, and DiffusionDB human evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including the single-reward, weighted multi-reward, Reward Soup, and heterogeneous-bound baselines in Tables 3 and 5. The human-study, VLM, and ReFL comparisons also retain their respective comparators.

E3.justification: Training settings, evaluation metrics, sample counts, and testing procedures are identical. Both retain SD3.5-Turbo, 50 candidates per prompt for frontier construction, and the same 300-prompt, ten-annotator human-study protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 7, heuristic detection analyses in Tables 8–9, entropy-regularization sweep in Table 10, and appendix frontier and collapse case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same seed-related statements and reward-distribution reporting, including standard deviations in Tables 8–9 and box plots in Figures 7–8. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 3 reports PG-OT JDR2 of 47.98%, JDR4 of 17.10%, and JCR4 of 2.39% in both versions; human-study and appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The Pareto and JDR/JCR definitions, optimal-transport equations, and Appendix C definitions, assumptions, and Proposition C.3 are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about reward hacking, heterogeneous reward bounds, PG-OT, JDR/JCR, and empirical advantages. No contribution is strengthened, narrowed, or redefined.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental results, Appendix D.4 discussion of heuristic detection limitations, and Appendix E applicability and scalability arguments are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are identical, including LoRA/DRaFT-K settings, agent evaluation intervals, GPU hardware, optimizer settings, runtime, and costs. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The reference list, introduction citations, and Appendix B related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to earlier reward optimization and Pareto-based methods remains identical.

P1.justification: Mohan Zhou and Yalong Bai gain Duxiaoman affiliation markers; Wenyi Mo's listed affiliation changes from Rutgers University to Duxiaoman, with corresponding affiliation renumbering. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised author and affiliation information causes limited first-page reflow and slightly shifts the abstract. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on PDF pages 2–23 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation metadata and first-page formatting while retaining all scientific content and evidence, including the appendices. These limited administrative changes do not materially alter the paper's scientific support, exposition, or reproducibility.
